newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA reaffirms Eskom ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA reaffirms Eskom ratings.

text.p: Rating agency IBCA on Wednesday reaffirmed electricity utility Eskom's short-term A1+ and long-term AAA domestic ratings as well as its long-term BBB international local currency rating.
The short- and long-term domestic ratings indicated the lowest expectation of investment risk and a substantial capacity for timely repayment of principal and interest, IBCA said in a statement.
The international local currency rating was the same as South Africa's sovereign local currency rating.

"Considering the maturity structure of the loan portfolio reduced capital expenditure and hence borrowing requirement, sufficient flexibility exists so as not to endanger repayment commitments," IBCA said.

Eskom's weighted average maturity period of net interest bearing debt is nine years, while its current surplus capacity is expected to be sufficient until 2006, putting a dampener on capital expenditure.

IBCA added that the majority of Eskom's foreign currency denominated borrowings were guaranteed by the State and, while local currency borrowings carried no guarantee, the importance which the utility had within the economy was likely to generate support, in need, from the State.
